quran.20:116: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِـَٔادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ
quran.20:117: فَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ إِنَّ هَٰذَا عَدُوٌّ لَّكَ وَلِزَوْجِكَ فَلَا يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَىٰٓ
quran.20:118: إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعْرَىٰ
quran.20:119: وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظْمَؤُا۟ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضْحَىٰ
quran.20:120: فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَّا يَبْلَىٰ
quran.20:121: فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَعَصَىٰٓ ءَادَمُ رَبَّهُۥ فَغَوَىٰ
quran.20:122: ثُمَّ ٱجْتَبَٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدَىٰ
quran.20:123: قَالَ ٱهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۢا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ
quran.21:51: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَآ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ رُشْدَهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا بِهِۦ عَٰلِمِينَ
quran.21:52: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنتُمْ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ
quran.21:54: قَالَ لَقَدْ كُنتُمْ أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُمْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
quran.21:55: قَالُوٓا۟ أَجِئْتَنَا بِٱلْحَقِّ أَمْ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱللَّٰعِبِينَ
quran.21:56: قَالَ بَل رَّبُّكُمْ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا۠ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
quran.21:57: وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَٰمَكُم بَعْدَ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ
quran.21:58: فَجَعَلَهُمْ جُذَٰذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرًا لَّهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ يَرْجِعُونَ
quran.21:59: قَالُوا۟ مَن فَعَلَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
quran.21:60: قَالُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهُمْ يُقَالُ لَهُۥٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ
quran.21:61: قَالُوا۟ فَأْتُوا۟ بِهِۦ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْيُنِ ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْهَدُونَ
quran.21:62: قَالُوٓا۟ ءَأَنتَ فَعَلْتَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَا يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ
quran.21:63: قَالَ بَلْ فَعَلَهُۥ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَٰذَا فَسْـَٔلُوهُمْ إِن كَانُوا۟ يَنطِقُونَ
quran.21:64: فَرَجَعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ فَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّكُمْ أَنتُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
quran.21:65: ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا۟ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمْ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ يَنطِقُونَ
quran.21:66: قَالَ أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمْ شَيْـًٔا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ
quran.21:67: أُفٍّ لَّكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
quran.21:68: قَالُوا۟ حَرِّقُوهُ وَٱنصُرُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ فَٰعِلِينَ
quran.21:69: قُلْنَا يَٰنَارُ كُونِى بَرْدًا وَسَلَٰمًا عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
quran.21:71: وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَلُوطًا إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّتِى بَٰرَكْنَا فِيهَا لِلْعَٰلَمِينَ
quran.21:72: وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةً وَكُلًّا جَعَلْنَا صَٰلِحِينَ
quran.21:73: وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِمْ فِعْلَ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَإِقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَإِيتَآءَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةِ وَكَانُوا۟ لَنَا عَٰبِدِينَ
quran.21:91: وَٱلَّتِىٓ أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهَا مِن رُّوحِنَا وَجَعَلْنَٰهَا وَٱبْنَهَآ ءَايَةً لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
quran.22:26: وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لِإِبْرَٰهِيمَ مَكَانَ ٱلْبَيْتِ أَن لَّا تُشْرِكْ بِى شَيْـًٔا وَطَهِّرْ بَيْتِىَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلْقَآئِمِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ
quran.22:27: وَأَذِّن فِى ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْحَجِّ يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالًا وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ يَأْتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ
quran.22:28: لِّيَشْهَدُوا۟ مَنَٰفِعَ لَهُمْ وَيَذْكُرُوا۟ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ فِىٓ أَيَّامٍ مَّعْلُومَٰتٍ عَلَىٰ مَا رَزَقَهُم مِّنۢ بَهِيمَةِ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ فَكُلُوا۟ مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا۟ ٱلْبَآئِسَ ٱلْفَقِيرَ
quran.22:29: ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا۟ تَفَثَهُمْ وَلْيُوفُوا۟ نُذُورَهُمْ وَلْيَطَّوَّفُوا۟ بِٱلْبَيْتِ ٱلْعَتِيقِ
quran.23:23: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ فَقَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥٓ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
quran.23:24: فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتَفَضَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَنزَلَ مَلَٰٓئِكَةً مَّا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِىٓ ءَابَآئِنَا ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
quran.23:25: إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا رَجُلٌۢ بِهِۦ جِنَّةٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا۟ بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ
quran.23:27: فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ
quran.23:28: فَإِذَا ٱسْتَوَيْتَ أَنتَ وَمَن مَّعَكَ عَلَى ٱلْفُلْكِ فَقُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى نَجَّىٰنَا مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
quran.23:29: وَقُل رَّبِّ أَنزِلْنِى مُنزَلًا مُّبَارَكًا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْمُنزِلِينَ
quran.23:30: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَٰتٍ وَإِن كُنَّا لَمُبْتَلِينَ
quran.23:45: ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَأَخَاهُ هَٰرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَسُلْطَٰنٍ مُّبِينٍ
quran.23:46: إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَإِي۟هِۦ فَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا عَالِينَ
quran.23:47: فَقَالُوٓا۟ أَنُؤْمِنُ لِبَشَرَيْنِ مِثْلِنَا وَقَوْمُهُمَا لَنَا عَٰبِدُونَ
quran.23:50: وَجَعَلْنَا ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُۥٓ ءَايَةً وَءَاوَيْنَٰهُمَآ إِلَىٰ رَبْوَةٍ ذَاتِ قَرَارٍ وَمَعِينٍ
quran.25:32: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ جُمْلَةً وَٰحِدَةً كَذَٰلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِۦ فُؤَادَكَ وَرَتَّلْنَٰهُ تَرْتِيلًا
quran.26:10: وَإِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبُّكَ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱئْتِ ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
quran.26:12: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
quran.26:13: وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ
quran.26:14: وَلَهُمْ عَلَىَّ ذَنۢبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ
quran.26:15: قَالَ كَلَّا فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ
quran.26:16: فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
quran.26:18: قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًا وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ
quran.26:19: وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِى فَعَلْتَ وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
quran.26:20: قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَآ إِذًا وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
quran.26:21: فَفَرَرْتُ مِنكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِى رَبِّى حُكْمًا وَجَعَلَنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
quran.26:22: وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَىَّ أَنْ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
quran.26:24: قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ
quran.26:27: قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌ
quran.26:28: قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَٱلْمَغْرِبِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ
quran.26:29: قَالَ لَئِنِ ٱتَّخَذْتَ إِلَٰهًا غَيْرِى لَأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمَسْجُونِينَ
quran.26:31: قَالَ فَأْتِ بِهِۦٓ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
quran.26:32: فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُّبِينٌ
quran.26:33: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ
quran.26:34: قَالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُۥٓ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
quran.26:35: يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِۦ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ
quran.26:36: قَالُوٓا۟ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبْعَثْ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
quran.26:40: لَعَلَّنَا نَتَّبِعُ ٱلسَّحَرَةَ إِن كَانُوا۟ هُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ
quran.26:41: فَلَمَّا جَآءَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ قَالُوا۟ لِفِرْعَوْنَ أَئِنَّ لَنَا لَأَجْرًا إِن كُنَّا نَحْنُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ
quran.26:42: قَالَ نَعَمْ وَإِنَّكُمْ إِذًا لَّمِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ
quran.26:43: قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰٓ أَلْقُوا۟ مَآ أَنتُم مُّلْقُونَ
quran.26:44: فَأَلْقَوْا۟ حِبَالَهُمْ وَعِصِيَّهُمْ وَقَالُوا۟ بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ
quran.26:45: فَأَلْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ تَلْقَفُ مَا يَأْفِكُونَ
quran.26:49: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
quran.26:50: قَالُوا۟ لَا ضَيْرَ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ
quran.26:51: إِنَّا نَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ لَنَا رَبُّنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَآ أَن كُنَّآ أَوَّلَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
quran.26:52: وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِىٓ إِنَّكُم مُّتَّبَعُونَ
quran.26:61: فَلَمَّا تَرَٰٓءَا ٱلْجَمْعَانِ قَالَ أَصْحَٰبُ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ
quran.26:62: قَالَ كَلَّآ إِنَّ مَعِىَ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ
quran.26:63: فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَٱنفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍ كَٱلطَّوْدِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
quran.26:67: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
quran.26:70: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ
quran.26:71: قَالُوا۟ نَعْبُدُ أَصْنَامًا فَنَظَلُّ لَهَا عَٰكِفِينَ
quran.26:74: قَالُوا۟ بَلْ وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا كَذَٰلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ
quran.26:77: فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِّىٓ إِلَّا رَبَّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
quran.26:82: وَٱلَّذِىٓ أَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ لِى خَطِيٓـَٔتِى يَوْمَ ٱلدِّينِ
quran.26:83: رَبِّ هَبْ لِى حُكْمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِى بِٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
quran.26:84: وَٱجْعَل لِّى لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرِينَ
quran.26:86: وَٱغْفِرْ لِأَبِىٓ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
quran.26:88: يَوْمَ لَا يَنفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ
quran.26:89: إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى ٱللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ
quran.26:92: وَقِيلَ لَهُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْبُدُونَ
quran.26:93: مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ هَلْ يَنصُرُونَكُمْ أَوْ يَنتَصِرُونَ
quran.26:97: تَٱللَّهِ إِن كُنَّا لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
quran.26:102: فَلَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً فَنَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
quran.26:103: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
quran.26:106: إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ نُوحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
quran.26:109: وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
quran.26:112: قَالَ وَمَا عِلْمِى بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
quran.26:113: إِنْ حِسَابُهُمْ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّى لَوْ تَشْعُرُونَ
quran.26:116: قَالُوا۟ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ يَٰنُوحُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمَرْجُومِينَ
quran.26:118: فَٱفْتَحْ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحًا وَنَجِّنِى وَمَن مَّعِىَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
quran.26:119: فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ
quran.26:121: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
quran.27:7: إِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِأَهْلِهِۦٓ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا سَـَٔاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ ءَاتِيكُم بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ
quran.27:8: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهَا نُودِىَ أَنۢ بُورِكَ مَن فِى ٱلنَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا وَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
quran.27:9: يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
quran.27:10: وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَا تَخَفْ إِنِّى لَا يَخَافُ لَدَىَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
quran.27:11: إِلَّا مَن ظَلَمَ ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْنًۢا بَعْدَ سُوٓءٍ فَإِنِّى غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
quran.27:12: وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ فِى تِسْعِ ءَايَٰتٍ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ
quran.28:3: نَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْكَ مِن نَّبَإِ مُوسَىٰ وَفِرْعَوْنَ بِٱلْحَقِّ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ
quran.28:4: إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ عَلَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَجَعَلَ أَهْلَهَا شِيَعًا يَسْتَضْعِفُ طَآئِفَةً مِّنْهُمْ يُذَبِّحُ أَبْنَآءَهُمْ وَيَسْتَحْىِۦ نِسَآءَهُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ
quran.28:5: وَنُرِيدُ أَن نَّمُنَّ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتُضْعِفُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَنَجْعَلَهُمْ أَئِمَّةً وَنَجْعَلَهُمُ ٱلْوَٰرِثِينَ
quran.28:6: وَنُمَكِّنَ لَهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَنُرِىَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا مِنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَحْذَرُونَ
quran.28:7: وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِى وَلَا تَحْزَنِىٓ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
quran.28:8: فَٱلْتَقَطَهُۥٓ ءَالُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَنًا إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰطِـِٔينَ
quran.28:9: وَقَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِّى وَلَكَ لَا تَقْتُلُوهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
quran.28:10: وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَٰرِغًا إِن كَادَتْ لَتُبْدِى بِهِۦ لَوْلَآ أَن رَّبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قَلْبِهَا لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
quran.28:11: وَقَالَتْ لِأُخْتِهِۦ قُصِّيهِ فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِۦ عَن جُنُبٍ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
quran.28:12: وَحَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَرَاضِعَ مِن قَبْلُ فَقَالَتْ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكْفُلُونَهُۥ لَكُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُۥ نَٰصِحُونَ
quran.28:13: فَرَدَدْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّهِۦ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَلِتَعْلَمَ أَنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
quran.28:14: وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَٱسْتَوَىٰٓ ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
quran.28:15: وَدَخَلَ ٱلْمَدِينَةَ عَلَىٰ حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَا فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلَانِ هَٰذَا مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ وَهَٰذَا مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَٱسْتَغَٰثَهُ ٱلَّذِى مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ عَلَى ٱلَّذِى مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَوَكَزَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ إِنَّهُۥ عَدُوٌّ مُّضِلٌّ مُّبِينٌ
quran.28:16: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِى فَٱغْفِرْ لِى فَغَفَرَ لَهُۥٓ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
quran.28:17: قَالَ رَبِّ بِمَآ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَىَّ فَلَنْ أَكُونَ ظَهِيرًا لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ
quran.28:18: فَأَصْبَحَ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ خَآئِفًا يَتَرَقَّبُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِى ٱسْتَنصَرَهُۥ بِٱلْأَمْسِ يَسْتَصْرِخُهُۥ قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّكَ لَغَوِىٌّ مُّبِينٌ
quran.28:19: فَلَمَّآ أَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَبْطِشَ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ عَدُوٌّ لَّهُمَا قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَتُرِيدُ أَن تَقْتُلَنِى كَمَا قَتَلْتَ نَفْسًۢا بِٱلْأَمْسِ إِن تُرِيدُ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ جَبَّارًا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا تُرِيدُ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِينَ
quran.28:20: وَجَآءَ رَجُلٌ مِّنْ أَقْصَا ٱلْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱلْمَلَأَ يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقْتُلُوكَ فَٱخْرُجْ إِنِّى لَكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ
quran.28:21: فَخَرَجَ مِنْهَا خَآئِفًا يَتَرَقَّبُ قَالَ رَبِّ نَجِّنِى مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
quran.28:22: وَلَمَّا تَوَجَّهَ تِلْقَآءَ مَدْيَنَ قَالَ عَسَىٰ رَبِّىٓ أَن يَهْدِيَنِى سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
quran.28:23: وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَآءَ مَدْيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ يَسْقُونَ وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمْرَأَتَيْنِ تَذُودَانِ قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُمَا قَالَتَا لَا نَسْقِى حَتَّىٰ يُصْدِرَ ٱلرِّعَآءُ وَأَبُونَا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ
quran.28:24: فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى لِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ إِلَىَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ
quran.28:25: فَجَآءَتْهُ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا تَمْشِى عَلَى ٱسْتِحْيَآءٍ قَالَتْ إِنَّ أَبِى يَدْعُوكَ لِيَجْزِيَكَ أَجْرَ مَا سَقَيْتَ لَنَا فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُۥ وَقَصَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَصَصَ قَالَ لَا تَخَفْ نَجَوْتَ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
quran.28:26: قَالَتْ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱسْتَـْٔجِرْهُ إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ ٱسْتَـْٔجَرْتَ ٱلْقَوِىُّ ٱلْأَمِينُ
quran.28:27: قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُنكِحَكَ إِحْدَى ٱبْنَتَىَّ هَٰتَيْنِ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَأْجُرَنِى ثَمَٰنِىَ حِجَجٍ فَإِنْ أَتْمَمْتَ عَشْرًا فَمِنْ عِندِكَ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشُقَّ عَلَيْكَ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
quran.28:28: قَالَ ذَٰلِكَ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَكَ أَيَّمَا ٱلْأَجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ فَلَا عُدْوَٰنَ عَلَىَّ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ
quran.28:29: فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلْأَجَلَ وَسَارَ بِأَهْلِهِۦٓ ءَانَسَ مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ نَارًا قَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوٓا۟ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ
quran.28:30: فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِىَ مِن شَٰطِئِ ٱلْوَادِ ٱلْأَيْمَنِ فِى ٱلْبُقْعَةِ ٱلْمُبَٰرَكَةِ مِنَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ أَن يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنِّىٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
quran.28:31: وَأَنْ أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَقْبِلْ وَلَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْـَٔامِنِينَ
quran.28:32: ٱسْلُكْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ وَٱضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ ٱلرَّهْبِ فَذَٰنِكَ بُرْهَٰنَانِ مِن رَّبِّكَ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَإِي۟هِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ
quran.28:33: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى قَتَلْتُ مِنْهُمْ نَفْسًا فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ
quran.28:34: وَأَخِى هَٰرُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّى لِسَانًا فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِىَ رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِىٓ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
quran.28:35: قَالَ سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلْطَٰنًا فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيْكُمَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أَنتُمَا وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكُمَا ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ
quran.28:36: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم مُّوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا بَيِّنَٰتٍ قَالُوا۟ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُّفْتَرًى وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِىٓ ءَابَآئِنَا ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
quran.28:37: وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ رَبِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن جَآءَ بِٱلْهُدَىٰ مِنْ عِندِهِۦ وَمَن تَكُونُ لَهُۥ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلدَّارِ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
quran.28:38: وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَأُ مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى فَأَوْقِدْ لِى يَٰهَٰمَٰنُ عَلَى ٱلطِّينِ فَٱجْعَل لِّى صَرْحًا لَّعَلِّىٓ أَطَّلِعُ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّى لَأَظُنُّهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
quran.28:39: وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ هُوَ وَجُنُودُهُۥ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ وَظَنُّوٓا۟ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْنَا لَا يُرْجَعُونَ
quran.28:40: فَأَخَذْنَٰهُ وَجُنُودَهُۥ فَنَبَذْنَٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
quran.28:41: وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَدْعُونَ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ وَيَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ لَا يُنصَرُونَ
quran.28:42: وَأَتْبَعْنَٰهُمْ فِى هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنْيَا لَعْنَةً وَيَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ هُم مِّنَ ٱلْمَقْبُوحِينَ
quran.29:14: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عَامًا فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلطُّوفَانُ وَهُمْ ظَٰلِمُونَ
quran.29:15: فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَأَصْحَٰبَ ٱلسَّفِينَةِ وَجَعَلْنَٰهَآ ءَايَةً لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
quran.29:16: وَإِبْرَٰهِيمَ إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱتَّقُوهُ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
quran.29:17: إِنَّمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْثَٰنًا وَتَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكًا إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ لَكُمْ رِزْقًا فَٱبْتَغُوا۟ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرِّزْقَ وَٱعْبُدُوهُ وَٱشْكُرُوا۟ لَهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
quran.29:24: فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوا۟ ٱقْتُلُوهُ أَوْ حَرِّقُوهُ فَأَنجَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَٰتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ
quran.29:25: وَقَالَ إِنَّمَا ٱتَّخَذْتُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْثَٰنًا مَّوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكُمْ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا ثُمَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ يَكْفُرُ بَعْضُكُم بِبَعْضٍ وَيَلْعَنُ بَعْضُكُم بَعْضًا وَمَأْوَىٰكُمُ ٱلنَّارُ وَمَا لَكُم مِّن نَّٰصِرِينَ
quran.29:26: فَـَٔامَنَ لَهُۥ لُوطٌ وَقَالَ إِنِّى مُهَاجِرٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّىٓ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
quran.29:27: وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَجَعَلْنَا فِى ذُرِّيَّتِهِ ٱلنُّبُوَّةَ وَٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ أَجْرَهُۥ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَإِنَّهُۥ فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
quran.33:40: مَّا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبَآ أَحَدٍ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ وَلَٰكِن رَّسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَخَاتَمَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمًا
quran.37:85: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَاذَا تَعْبُدُونَ
quran.37:91: فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ ءَالِهَتِهِمْ فَقَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ
quran.37:97: قَالُوا۟ ٱبْنُوا۟ لَهُۥ بُنْيَٰنًا فَأَلْقُوهُ فِى ٱلْجَحِيمِ
quran.37:99: وَقَالَ إِنِّى ذَاهِبٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ
quran.37:102: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعْىَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ فِى ٱلْمَنَامِ أَنِّىٓ أَذْبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
quran.37:105: قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ ٱلرُّءْيَآ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
quran.37:113: وَبَٰرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَىٰٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحْسِنٌ وَظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِۦ مُبِينٌ
quran.38:71: إِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى خَٰلِقٌۢ بَشَرًا مِّن طِينٍ
quran.38:72: فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُۥ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِى فَقَعُوا۟ لَهُۥ سَٰجِدِينَ
quran.38:74: إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ ٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
quran.38:75: قَالَ يَٰٓإِبْلِيسُ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَن تَسْجُدَ لِمَا خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَىَّ أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ أَمْ كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلْعَالِينَ
quran.38:76: قَالَ أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍ
quran.38:78: وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ لَعْنَتِىٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ
quran.38:79: قَالَ رَبِّ فَأَنظِرْنِىٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
quran.38:85: لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكَ وَمِمَّن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
quran.40:23: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَسُلْطَٰنٍ مُّبِينٍ
quran.40:24: إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَقَٰرُونَ فَقَالُوا۟ سَٰحِرٌ كَذَّابٌ
quran.40:25: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِٱلْحَقِّ مِنْ عِندِنَا قَالُوا۟ ٱقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَبْنَآءَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ وَٱسْتَحْيُوا۟ نِسَآءَهُمْ وَمَا كَيْدُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ
quran.40:26: وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ ذَرُونِىٓ أَقْتُلْ مُوسَىٰ وَلْيَدْعُ رَبَّهُۥٓ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُبَدِّلَ دِينَكُمْ أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
quran.40:27: وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنِّى عُذْتُ بِرَبِّى وَرَبِّكُم مِّن كُلِّ مُتَكَبِّرٍ لَّا يُؤْمِنُ بِيَوْمِ ٱلْحِسَابِ
quran.40:28: وَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مُّؤْمِنٌ مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَكْتُمُ إِيمَٰنَهُۥٓ أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ وَقَدْ جَآءَكُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ مِن رَّبِّكُمْ وَإِن يَكُ كَٰذِبًا فَعَلَيْهِ كَذِبُهُۥ وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقًا يُصِبْكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِى يَعِدُكُمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ كَذَّابٌ
quran.40:34: وَلَقَدْ جَآءَكُمْ يُوسُفُ مِن قَبْلُ بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ فَمَا زِلْتُمْ فِى شَكٍّ مِّمَّا جَآءَكُم بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا هَلَكَ قُلْتُمْ لَن يَبْعَثَ ٱللَّهُ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ رَسُولًا كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ مُّرْتَابٌ
quran.43:57: وَلَمَّا ضُرِبَ ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ مَثَلًا إِذَا قَوْمُكَ مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ
quran.43:58: وَقَالُوٓا۟ ءَأَٰلِهَتُنَا خَيْرٌ أَمْ هُوَ مَا ضَرَبُوهُ لَكَ إِلَّا جَدَلًۢا بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ خَصِمُونَ
quran.43:59: إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا عَبْدٌ أَنْعَمْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَجَعَلْنَٰهُ مَثَلًا لِّبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
quran.43:60: وَلَوْ نَشَآءُ لَجَعَلْنَا مِنكُم مَّلَٰٓئِكَةً فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَخْلُفُونَ
quran.43:61: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَعِلْمٌ لِّلسَّاعَةِ فَلَا تَمْتَرُنَّ بِهَا وَٱتَّبِعُونِ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ
quran.43:62: وَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ إِنَّهُۥ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ
quran.43:63: وَلَمَّا جَآءَ عِيسَىٰ بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ قَالَ قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَلِأُبَيِّنَ لَكُم بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِى تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
quran.43:64: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ رَبِّى وَرَبُّكُمْ فَٱعْبُدُوهُ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ
quran.43:65: فَٱخْتَلَفَ ٱلْأَحْزَابُ مِنۢ بَيْنِهِمْ فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ
quran.44:3: إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ فِى لَيْلَةٍ مُّبَٰرَكَةٍ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ
quran.44:5: أَمْرًا مِّنْ عِندِنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ
quran.44:6: رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
quran.44:24: وَٱتْرُكِ ٱلْبَحْرَ رَهْوًا إِنَّهُمْ جُندٌ مُّغْرَقُونَ
quran.44:29: فَمَا بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ مُنظَرِينَ
quran.44:30: وَلَقَدْ نَجَّيْنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْمُهِينِ
quran.44:31: مِن فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَالِيًا مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ
quran.47:2: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَءَامَنُوا۟ بِمَا نُزِّلَ عَلَىٰ مُحَمَّدٍ وَهُوَ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمْ كَفَّرَ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمْ وَأَصْلَحَ بَالَهُمْ
quran.48:29: مُّحَمَّدٌ رَّسُولُ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلَّذِينَ مَعَهُۥٓ أَشِدَّآءُ عَلَى ٱلْكُفَّارِ رُحَمَآءُ بَيْنَهُمْ تَرَىٰهُمْ رُكَّعًا سُجَّدًا يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضْوَٰنًا سِيمَاهُمْ فِى وُجُوهِهِم مِّنْ أَثَرِ ٱلسُّجُودِ ذَٰلِكَ مَثَلُهُمْ فِى ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ وَمَثَلُهُمْ فِى ٱلْإِنجِيلِ كَزَرْعٍ أَخْرَجَ شَطْـَٔهُۥ فَـَٔازَرَهُۥ فَٱسْتَغْلَظَ فَٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَىٰ سُوقِهِۦ يُعْجِبُ ٱلزُّرَّاعَ لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ ٱلْكُفَّارَ وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ مِنْهُم مَّغْفِرَةً وَأَجْرًا عَظِيمًۢا
quran.51:24: هَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ
quran.51:25: إِذْ دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًا قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ
quran.51:26: فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ
quran.51:28: فَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ عَلِيمٍ
quran.51:29: فَأَقْبَلَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ فِى صَرَّةٍ فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ
quran.51:30: قَالُوا۟ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
quran.51:32: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّآ أُرْسِلْنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ مُّجْرِمِينَ
quran.51:35: فَأَخْرَجْنَا مَن كَانَ فِيهَا مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
quran.51:36: فَمَا وَجَدْنَا فِيهَا غَيْرَ بَيْتٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ
quran.51:37: وَتَرَكْنَا فِيهَآ ءَايَةً لِّلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلْأَلِيمَ
quran.54:9: كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ فَكَذَّبُوا۟ عَبْدَنَا وَقَالُوا۟ مَجْنُونٌ وَٱزْدُجِرَ
quran.54:12: وَفَجَّرْنَا ٱلْأَرْضَ عُيُونًا فَٱلْتَقَى ٱلْمَآءُ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ
quran.54:14: تَجْرِى بِأَعْيُنِنَا جَزَآءً لِّمَن كَانَ كُفِرَ
quran.54:15: وَلَقَد تَّرَكْنَٰهَآ ءَايَةً فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
quran.54:17: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
quran.57:27: ثُمَّ قَفَّيْنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم بِرُسُلِنَا وَقَفَّيْنَا بِعِيسَى ٱبْنِ مَرْيَمَ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ ٱلْإِنجِيلَ وَجَعَلْنَا فِى قُلُوبِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوهُ رَأْفَةً وَرَحْمَةً وَرَهْبَانِيَّةً ٱبْتَدَعُوهَا مَا كَتَبْنَٰهَا عَلَيْهِمْ إِلَّا ٱبْتِغَآءَ رِضْوَٰنِ ٱللَّهِ فَمَا رَعَوْهَا حَقَّ رِعَايَتِهَا فَـَٔاتَيْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ أَجْرَهُمْ وَكَثِيرٌ مِّنْهُمْ فَٰسِقُونَ
quran.60:4: قَدْ كَانَتْ لَكُمْ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ فِىٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَٱلَّذِينَ مَعَهُۥٓ إِذْ قَالُوا۟ لِقَوْمِهِمْ إِنَّا بُرَءَٰٓؤُا۟ مِنكُمْ وَمِمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَفَرْنَا بِكُمْ وَبَدَا بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمُ ٱلْعَدَٰوَةُ وَٱلْبَغْضَآءُ أَبَدًا حَتَّىٰ تُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ وَحْدَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَوْلَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ لَأَسْتَغْفِرَنَّ لَكَ وَمَآ أَمْلِكُ لَكَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ رَّبَّنَا عَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْنَا وَإِلَيْكَ أَنَبْنَا وَإِلَيْكَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ
quran.60:5: رَبَّنَا لَا تَجْعَلْنَا فِتْنَةً لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَٱغْفِرْ لَنَا رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
quran.60:6: لَقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِيهِمْ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ لِّمَن كَانَ يَرْجُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلْيَوْمَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْغَنِىُّ ٱلْحَمِيدُ
quran.61:5: وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦ يَٰقَوْمِ لِمَ تُؤْذُونَنِى وَقَد تَّعْلَمُونَ أَنِّى رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ فَلَمَّا زَاغُوٓا۟ أَزَاغَ ٱللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ
quran.61:6: وَإِذْ قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ إِنِّى رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَيْكُم مُّصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَىَّ مِنَ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ وَمُبَشِّرًۢا بِرَسُولٍ يَأْتِى مِنۢ بَعْدِى ٱسْمُهُۥٓ أَحْمَدُ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ
quran.61:14: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوٓا۟ أَنصَارَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَا قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ لِلْحَوَارِيِّـۧنَ مَنْ أَنصَارِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ قَالَ ٱلْحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنصَارُ ٱللَّهِ فَـَٔامَنَت طَّآئِفَةٌ مِّنۢ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَكَفَرَت طَّآئِفَةٌ فَأَيَّدْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ عَلَىٰ عَدُوِّهِمْ فَأَصْبَحُوا۟ ظَٰهِرِينَ
quran.66:12: وَمَرْيَمَ ٱبْنَتَ عِمْرَٰنَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِنَا وَصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِمَٰتِ رَبِّهَا وَكُتُبِهِۦ وَكَانَتْ مِنَ ٱلْقَٰنِتِينَ
quran.71:1: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦٓ أَنْ أَنذِرْ قَوْمَكَ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
quran.71:2: قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ إِنِّى لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ
quran.71:4: يَغْفِرْ لَكُم مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمْ وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى إِنَّ أَجَلَ ٱللَّهِ إِذَا جَآءَ لَا يُؤَخَّرُ لَوْ كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
quran.71:5: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى دَعَوْتُ قَوْمِى لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا
quran.71:7: وَإِنِّى كُلَّمَا دَعَوْتُهُمْ لِتَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ جَعَلُوٓا۟ أَصَٰبِعَهُمْ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ وَٱسْتَغْشَوْا۟ ثِيَابَهُمْ وَأَصَرُّوا۟ وَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ ٱسْتِكْبَارًا
quran.71:9: ثُمَّ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَنتُ لَهُمْ وَأَسْرَرْتُ لَهُمْ إِسْرَارًا
quran.71:10: فَقُلْتُ ٱسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفَّارًا
quran.71:12: وَيُمْدِدْكُم بِأَمْوَٰلٍ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجْعَل لَّكُمْ جَنَّٰتٍ وَيَجْعَل لَّكُمْ أَنْهَٰرًا
quran.71:13: مَّا لَكُمْ لَا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَارًا
quran.71:15: أَلَمْ تَرَوْا۟ كَيْفَ خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَمَٰوَٰتٍ طِبَاقًا
quran.71:16: وَجَعَلَ ٱلْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا وَجَعَلَ ٱلشَّمْسَ سِرَاجًا
quran.71:21: قَالَ نُوحٌ رَّبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِى وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ مَن لَّمْ يَزِدْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَوَلَدُهُۥٓ إِلَّا خَسَارًا
quran.71:23: وَقَالُوا۟ لَا تَذَرُنَّ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلَا سُوَاعًا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًا
quran.71:24: وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا۟ كَثِيرًا وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلَٰلًا
quran.71:25: مِّمَّا خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِهِمْ أُغْرِقُوا۟ فَأُدْخِلُوا۟ نَارًا فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا۟ لَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَنصَارًا
quran.71:26: وَقَالَ نُوحٌ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرْ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ دَيَّارًا
quran.71:27: إِنَّكَ إِن تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا۟ عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوٓا۟ إِلَّا فَاجِرًا كَفَّارًا
quran.71:28: رَّبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِى وَلِوَٰلِدَىَّ وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيْتِىَ مُؤْمِنًا وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارًۢا
quran.79:16: إِذْ نَادَىٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى
quran.79:18: فَقُلْ هَل لَّكَ إِلَىٰٓ أَن تَزَكَّىٰ
quran.79:26: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰٓ
quran.96:1: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ
quran.97:1: بِّسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ فِى لَيْلَةِ ٱلْقَدْرِ
quran.97:3: لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ
quran.97:4: تَنَزَّلُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍ

claims.statement_en: God created the human being from dry clay, from moulded mud.
God told the angels that He was going to create a human being from clay.
God said that when He had fashioned the human being and breathed into him of His spirit, the angels were to fall down before him in prostration.
The Quran likens the creation of Isa to that of Adam: God created Adam from dust, then said "Be", and he was.

chapters.summary_md: God told the angels that He would create a human being from clay, and that once he was fashioned and God had breathed into him of His spirit, they were to prostrate to him [c2][c3]. The Quran also likens the creation of Adam to that of Isa [c4].
chapters.body_md:
God told the angels that He was going to create a human being from clay [c2]. One passage calls it dry clay, taken from moulded mud [c1]. Once He had fashioned him and breathed into him of His spirit, the angels were to fall down before him in prostration [c3].

The Quran also speaks of Adam when it compares him with Isa: God created Adam from dust, then said "Be", and he was [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The passages use different words for the substance: dry clay from moulded mud [c1], clay [c2], and dust in the comparison with Isa [c4]. The passages at 15:28-29 and 38:71-72 speak of a human being and do not name Adam [c2][c3].
chapters.kids_md: God told the angels that He would make a human being from clay [c2]. When God had shaped him and breathed His spirit into him, the angels were told to prostrate to him, which means to bow right down [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that an origin in clay is a reminder of humility [c1]. Another is that the angels were told to honour the human being only by God's command and after God had fashioned him [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- The Quran does not give the time or place of Adam's creation, or Adam's age.
- The verses do not say how the words for his substance (dust, clay, dry clay, moulded mud) relate to one another.
- The exact sense of the Arabic phrases rendered 'dry clay' and 'moulded mud' is not given in the verses; this draft keeps the wording general.
- The passages at 15:28-29 and 38:71-72 do not name the human being. To read them as the same event as the prostration to Adam is an inference from matching wording; the event inventory makes the same link.
- The verses do not explain what 'His spirit' is or how the breathing happened.

claims.statement_en: God told the angels that He was placing a khalifah (a successor or steward) on the earth.
The angels asked whether He would place there someone who would spread corruption and shed blood, while they glorified Him with praise and declared Him holy.
God replied that He knows what they do not know.
God taught Adam the names, all of them.
God then presented them to the angels and told them to tell Him the names of these, if they were truthful.
The angels declared God glorious and said they had no knowledge except what He had taught them.
God told Adam to inform them of the names, and when Adam did, God said He had told them that He knows what is unseen in the heavens and the earth, and what they show and what they hide.

chapters.summary_md: God told the angels about a successor He was placing on the earth, the angels asked a question, and God taught Adam the names [c1][c2][c4]. Adam told the angels the names when God asked him to [c7].
chapters.body_md:
God told the angels that He was placing a successor, or steward (the Arabic word is khalifah), on the earth [c1]. The angels asked whether He would put there someone who would spread corruption and shed blood, while they themselves glorified Him with praise and declared Him holy [c2]. God replied that He knows what they do not know [c3].

Then God taught Adam all the names [c4] and presented them to the angels, telling them to give Him the names of these if they were truthful [c5]. The angels declared Him glorious and said they had no knowledge except what He had taught them [c6]. God told Adam to inform them of the names, and when Adam did so God said He had told them that He knows what is unseen in the heavens and the earth, and what they show and what they hide [c7].
chapters.deep_md: God's answer to the angels' question is that He knows what they do not know [c3]; the matter of the names follows [c4][c5]. The passage ends with the angels acknowledging that their knowledge is what God taught them [c6], and with God's reminder of His knowledge of the unseen [c7].
chapters.kids_md: God told the angels about a successor on the earth [c1]. The angels asked a question, and God said He knows what they do not [c2][c3]. God taught Adam the names, and Adam told them to the angels when God asked him to [c4][c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that a question put to God is answered here with the reply that God knows what the asker does not [c2][c3]. Another is that the angels, once shown, acknowledged that what they knew was what God had taught them [c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- The Quran does not say what the names were, what they were the names of, or how they were taught.
- It does not say whose successor the khalifah is, or whether the word means a successor, a steward or a ruler; this draft gives the Arabic word beside more than one rendering and decides nothing.
- These verses do not say how this scene stands in time to the creation described in other passages. The order of the chapters in this story is a reading order, not a chronology the Quran gives.

claims.statement_en: God told the angels to prostrate to Adam, and they prostrated.
All the angels prostrated, every one of them together.
Iblis did not prostrate: he refused, and was not among those who prostrated.
The Quran says that Iblis was arrogant and was among the disbelievers.
God asked Iblis what prevented him from prostrating when He had commanded him, and what was the matter that he was not with those who prostrated.
Iblis said that he was better than Adam, because he had been created from fire and Adam from clay; he said he would not prostrate to a human being God had created from dry clay of moulded mud.
God told Iblis to go out, saying he had no right to be arrogant there and was among the humiliated, that he was driven away, and that God's curse was on him until the Day of Judgement.

chapters.summary_md: God told the angels to prostrate to Adam, and all of them did, but Iblis refused, saying he was made of fire and Adam of clay [c1][c2][c3][c6]. God then told him to go out and said the curse would be on him until the Day of Judgement [c7].
chapters.body_md:
God commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, and they did [c1]. The Quran stresses that all of them did so together [c2]. Iblis did not; he refused and was not among those who prostrated [c3], and the Quran says he was arrogant and among the disbelievers [c4].

God asked Iblis what had prevented him from prostrating when he was commanded [c5]. Iblis replied that he was better than Adam, because he had been created from fire and Adam from clay [c6]. In another passage Iblis says he would not prostrate to a human being whom God had created from dry clay of moulded mud [c6].

God then told Iblis to go out, saying that he had no right to be arrogant there, that he was among the humiliated and driven away, and that the curse would be on him until the Day of Judgement [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The command and the prostration are told in more than one passage with different emphasis: the plain act [c1], that all the angels did it together [c2], Iblis's refusal [c3], and his arrogance [c4]. The questions put to Iblis differ in wording between passages: what prevented him from prostrating, or what was the matter that he was not with those who prostrated [c5].
chapters.kids_md: God told the angels to bow down to Adam, and they all did [c1][c2]. Iblis refused because he said he was better, being made of fire while Adam was made of clay [c3][c6]. God told him to go out [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage names pride as the reason given for the refusal: Iblis compares what he was made of with what Adam was made of [c4][c6]. One reading is a caution against judging worth by origin or material [c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- The Quran does not say where this scene took place, or what Iblis was told to go out from.
- It does not describe how the angels prostrated or what kind of prostration it was.
- These verses name Iblis as the one who refused among those addressed; they do not themselves say whether he was an angel or one of the jinn. A passage outside this draft's range (18:50) speaks to this, and a reviewer should decide whether to add it.
- It does not say how long the scene lasted or who else witnessed it.

claims.statement_en: Iblis asked God to give him respite until the day when people are raised, after God had addressed him by name and asked why he was not with those who prostrated.
God said that Iblis was among those given respite, until the "day of the known time".

Iblis said that, because God had led him astray, he would lie in wait for people on God's straight path, and then approach them from in front, from behind, from their right and from their left; he said most of them would not be thankful.
Iblis vowed to make wrongdoing look fair to people on the earth and to lead them all astray, except God's sincere servants.
God said that Iblis has no authority over His servants, except over those of the misled who follow him.
Hell is the promised place of all those who follow Iblis; it has seven gates, and each gate has a portion of them assigned to it.
God told Iblis to go out, disgraced and driven away, and said that He would fill Hell with Iblis and with those among people who follow him, all together.

chapters.summary_md: Iblis asked for respite until the day people are raised, and God granted it [c1][c2]. Iblis vowed to lead people astray except God's sincere servants, and God said he has no authority over His servants apart from those who follow him [c4][c5].
chapters.body_md:
Iblis asked God to give him respite until the day when people are raised [c1]. God granted it, saying that he was among those given respite until the "day of the known time" [c2].

Iblis then said that, because God had led him astray, he would lie in wait for people on God's straight path and come at them from in front, from behind, from their right and from their left, and that most of them would not be thankful [c3]. In the parallel passages he vows to make wrongdoing look fair to people on the earth and to lead them all astray, except God's sincere servants [c4].

God replied that Iblis has no authority over His servants, except over those of the misled who follow him [c5]. He told Iblis to go out, disgraced and driven away, and said that He would fill Hell with Iblis and with those among people who follow him [c7]. Hell is the promised place of all those who follow him; it has seven gates, each with a portion of them assigned to it [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The request, the grant and the vow appear in more than one passage with small differences [c1][c2][c4]. In one passage Iblis speaks of lying in wait on the straight path [c3]; in the others he speaks of making wrongdoing look fair on the earth [c4]. The time of the respite is given as the "day of the known time" [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Iblis asked God to let him wait until the day people are raised, and God allowed it [c1][c2]. Iblis said he would try to lead people astray [c3][c4]. God said he has no authority over God's servants, except those who follow him [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage records Iblis's own announcement that he will try to mislead people [c3][c4], and records a limit on him: no authority over God's servants except those who follow him [c5]. One reading is a reminder to be on guard [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- The Quran does not say when the 'day of the known time' is.
- It does not describe how Iblis 'lies in wait' or comes from the directions he names; the verses give his words only.
- What Iblis means by saying that God led him astray is not explained in these verses.
- Hell is described here only by its seven gates and their portions; the verses give no further description of it.

chapters.title_en: The garden and the one limit

claims.statement_en: God told Adam to live in the garden with his wife and to eat from it freely, wherever they wished.
God told them not to approach a certain tree, or they would be among the wrongdoers.
God told Adam that the one who had refused to prostrate was an enemy to him and to his wife, and that he must not let that enemy drive them out of the garden, or Adam would be in hardship.
God said that in the garden Adam would not go hungry or be without clothing, and would not be thirsty or suffer from the sun's heat.

chapters.summary_md: God settled Adam and his wife in the garden, let them eat freely, and set one limit: not to approach a particular tree [c1][c2]. He warned them about the one who had refused to prostrate [c3].
chapters.body_md:
God told Adam to live in the garden with his wife and to eat from it freely, wherever they wished [c1]. There was one limit: they were not to approach a certain tree, or they would be among the wrongdoers [c2].

God also warned Adam that the one who had refused to prostrate was an enemy to him and to his wife, and that he must not let that enemy drive them out of the garden, or Adam would be in hardship [c3]. In the garden, God said, Adam would not go hungry or be without clothing, and would not be thirsty or suffer from the sun's heat [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The command at 2:35 and the command at 7:19 are worded almost alike: live in the garden, eat, and do not approach this tree [c1][c2]. The passage at 20:116-119 adds the warning about the enemy and a description of the garden as a place without hunger, thirst, lack of clothing or heat [c3][c4].
chapters.kids_md: God let Adam and his wife live in the garden and eat from it freely [c1]. God told them not to go near one tree [c2]. God also warned them about the enemy who had refused to bow down [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The account joins wide freedom with one clear limit [c1][c2]. One reading is that the warning came before the mistake, not after it [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- The Quran does not say which tree it was or what kind of plant; it says 'this tree' only. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: some later accounts name a particular fruit or grain for the tree; none is given in these verses.
- It does not name Adam's wife. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Hawwa (in English, Eve).
- It does not say where the garden was, whether it was on the earth or elsewhere, or how long Adam and his wife stayed in it.
- The warning at 20:117 says 'this' enemy; it is read as the one who refused to prostrate from the verse just before it.

claims.statement_en: Satan whispered to them, to make visible to them what had been hidden from them of their nakedness.
Satan told them that their Lord had forbidden them this tree only so that they would not become angels or be among those who live forever.
Satan swore to them that he was a sincere adviser to them.
Satan whispered to Adam, asking whether he should show him the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay.
They ate from the tree, and their nakedness became visible to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves of the garden.
God called to them, asking whether He had not forbidden them that tree and told them that Satan was a clear enemy to them.
The Quran says Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray.
The Quran says Satan led them down by deception.
God had made a covenant with Adam beforehand; Adam forgot, and God found in him no firm resolve.

chapters.summary_md: Satan whispered to Adam and his wife and led them down by deception; they ate from the tree, saw that they were uncovered, and began to cover themselves with leaves [c1][c5][c8]. God reminded them of His warning [c6].
chapters.body_md:
The Quran says Satan whispered to them [c1]. He told them that their Lord had forbidden them this tree only so that they would not become angels or be among those who live forever [c2], and he swore to them that he was giving them sincere advice [c3]. In the account at 20:120 he asks Adam whether he should show him the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay [c4]. The Quran says Satan led them down by deception [c8].

They ate from the tree, and what had been hidden of their nakedness became visible to them [c5]. They began to cover themselves with leaves of the garden [c5]. God called to them, asking whether He had not forbidden them that tree and told them that Satan was a clear enemy to them [c6].

The Quran says Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray [c7]. It also says that God had made a covenant with Adam beforehand, and that he forgot, and God found in him no firm resolve [c9].
chapters.deep_md: The accounts at 7:20 and 20:120 give different words to Satan: at 7:20 he speaks of angels and of living forever [c2], at 20:120 of the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay [c4]. The passage at 20:115 sets the event against an earlier covenant and a lapse of memory [c9].
chapters.kids_md: Satan whispered to Adam and his wife and tricked them [c1][c8]. They ate from the tree God had told them to keep away from [c5]. They saw they were uncovered and began to cover themselves with leaves [c5]. God reminded them that Satan was a clear enemy [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage shows temptation arriving as a promise of something good: living forever, or a kingdom that does not decay [c2][c4]. One reading is the value of holding to a clear instruction even when a persuasive voice offers more [c2][c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- The Quran does not say which tree it was; it says only 'this tree' and, in Satan's words, 'the tree of eternity'.
- It does not say how Satan spoke to them, or in what form; the verses record his words only.
- The Quran uses the words 'disobeyed' and 'went astray' for the act and also says Adam forgot and had no firm resolve. How this is to be understood theologically is not explained in these verses and is left to the scholarly reviewer.
- It does not say how long the stay in the garden lasted before this happened.

claims.statement_en: Satan caused them to slip and brought them out of the state they were in.
Adam received words from his Lord, and God accepted his repentance; He is the one who accepts repentance and is merciful.
Adam and his wife said that they had wronged themselves, and that if God did not forgive them and have mercy on them they would be among the losers.
God chose Adam, accepted his repentance and guided him.
God told them to go down, some of them enemies of others, and said that on the earth they would have a place to live and provision for a time.
God said that on the earth they would live, on it they would die, and from it they would be brought out.
God said that guidance would come to them from Him, and that whoever follows it will have no fear and will not grieve, and will not go astray or be wretched.
Those who disbelieve and deny God's signs are the companions of the Fire, there to remain.

chapters.summary_md: Adam and his wife asked God to forgive them, and God accepted Adam's repentance, chose him and guided him [c2][c3][c4]. They were told to go down to the earth, where they would live for a time, and God said guidance would come to them [c5][c7].
chapters.body_md:
Satan caused them to slip and brought them out of the state they had been in [c1]. Adam and his wife said that they had wronged themselves, and that unless God forgave them and had mercy on them they would be among the losers [c3]. Adam received words from his Lord, and God accepted his repentance [c2]; the Quran also says that God chose him, accepted his repentance and guided him [c4].

God told them to go down, some of them enemies of others, and said that on the earth they would have a place to live and provision for a time [c5]. On it they would live, on it they would die, and from it they would be brought out [c6].

God said that guidance would come to them from Him [c7]. Whoever follows that guidance will have no fear and will not grieve, and will not go astray or be wretched [c7]. Those who disbelieve and deny God's signs are the companions of the Fire, there to remain [c8].
chapters.deep_md: The repentance appears in the plain statement that God accepted it [c2], in the words of the pair themselves [c3], and in the report that God chose Adam and guided him [c4]. The command to go down is joined to the promise of guidance, worded slightly differently at 2:38 and 20:123 [c7].
chapters.kids_md: Adam and his wife said they had wronged themselves and asked God to forgive them and have mercy on them [c3]. God accepted Adam's repentance [c2]. God told them to go down to the earth and live there for a time, and said guidance would come to them [c5][c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): In the text the account of the slip is followed by repentance, acceptance and guidance [c2][c4]. One reading is that returning to God is presented as open after a mistake [c2][c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- The Quran does not say what the 'words' Adam received were.
- It does not say where on the earth they came down, how they came down, or how they were separated or brought together afterwards.
- These verses attribute the plea for forgiveness to both Adam and his wife (7:23), and the acceptance of repentance to Adam (2:37, 20:122); they do not say more about her part.
- They do not give any date or duration for the descent.
- The Arabic pronoun in 2:36 ('from it') can refer to the tree or to the garden; this draft does not decide.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the creation of Adam, the prostration and the garden. None is used in this draft.
Adam's status as a prophet comes from later tradition; the cited verses speak of God choosing and guiding him but do not use the word prophet of him. A scholar should decide how to word it.
The passages at 15:28-29 and 38:71-72 speak of a human being without the name; they are read here as the same event as the prostration to Adam (an inference, as in the event inventory).
The word khalifah (2:30) is left with more than one rendering; its sense is for the reviewer.

Whether Iblis was an angel or one of the jinn is addressed by 18:50, outside the range of this draft. The inventory range also includes 15:27 (the creation of the jinn) and 15:41 (a statement by God about a straight path); neither is used in the story texts, which describe neither angels nor jinn and avoid a disputed sentence, and a reviewer should decide whether they belong.

The chapters follow a reading order (creation, the question of the angels, the prostration, the respite, the garden, the slip, repentance and descent). The Quran does not give a chronology across these surahs.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of Adam's wife and the kind of the tree. Neither is used in the story texts.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

claims.statement_en: God sent Nuh to his people; one passage calls him their brother.
Nuh told them to worship God, for they had no deity other than Him.
Nuh told them to fear God and to obey him.
God told Nuh to warn his people before a painful punishment came to them.
Nuh told them that he feared for them the punishment of a great day, and of a painful day.
Nuh described himself to them as a plain warner and as a trustworthy messenger.
Nuh told them that he asked them for no reward for it, and that his reward was with the Lord of the worlds.
Nuh told them that if they obeyed, God would forgive them some of their sins and give them time until a stated term, and that God's term, when it comes, is not put back.
The Quran says that the people of Nuh denied the messengers.

chapters.summary_md: God sent Nuh to his people to call them to worship God alone; he warned them of a coming punishment and asked no reward [c1][c2][c4][c7].
chapters.body_md:
God sent Nuh to his people; one passage calls him their brother [c1]. He told them to worship God, since they had no deity other than Him [c2], to fear God and to obey him [c3]. God told Nuh to warn his people before a painful punishment came to them [c4], and Nuh told them that he feared for them the punishment of a great day [c5].

Nuh described himself as a plain warner and a trustworthy messenger [c6]. He told them that he asked them for no reward, because his reward was with the Lord of the worlds [c7]. He also told them that if they obeyed, God would forgive them some of their sins and allow them time until a stated term, and that God's term, once it comes, is not put back [c8]. The Quran says that the people of Nuh denied the messengers [c9].
chapters.deep_md: The same call appears in more than one place (7:59, 11:26, 23:23 and 71:3) with the same core: worship God and fear Him [c2][c3]. The description of the punishment differs by passage: a great day (7:59), a painful day (11:26), a painful punishment (71:1) [c4][c5].
chapters.kids_md: God sent Nuh to his people [c1]. He told them to worship God alone, to be mindful of God, and to obey him [c2][c3]. He warned them of a punishment to come, and he did not ask them for any reward [c4][c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The Quran presents Nuh as a caller who warns and asks for nothing in return [c4][c7]. One reading is that sincerity in giving advice is shown by not asking for gain from it [c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- The Quran does not say when or where Nuh lived, how many people were in his community, or what their land was called.
- It does not give Nuh's family line or his age when he was sent.
- It does not describe what the people worshipped before Nuh came, beyond the names given in 71:23 (see the chapter on the long call).
- The passage at 26:105 speaks of 'the messengers' in the plural although it concerns Nuh's people; the verse does not explain this wording.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later accounts give Nuh a lineage and names for his family; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: The leaders of Nuh's people said that they saw him in clear error.
Nuh replied that he was not in error but was a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, delivering his Lord's messages, advising them, and knowing from God what they did not know.
Nuh asked whether they were astonished that a reminder from their Lord had come on a man from among them, to warn them.
The leaders who disbelieved said that they saw him only as a human being like themselves.
They said that only the lowliest among them followed him, and asked whether they should believe him when the lowliest followed him.
They said that he wished to gain superiority over them, that God would have sent down angels if He had willed, and that they had not heard of such a thing among their forefathers.
They said that he was only a man with madness, and that they should wait for him for a time.
Another passage says that they called Nuh mad and that he was driven off.
Nuh said that he was on a clear proof from his Lord and had been given mercy from Him, which had been hidden from them, and asked whether he could force it on them while they disliked it.
Nuh said that he asked them for no wealth for it, that his reward was only with God, and that he would not drive away the believers, who would meet their Lord.
Nuh asked who would help him against God if he drove the believers away.

Nuh said that he did not claim to hold God's treasures, did not know the unseen, and did not claim to be an angel, and that he would not say that God would never give good to those whom they looked down on.
Nuh said that he had no knowledge of what they used to do, that their reckoning was only with his Lord, and that he was only a plain warner.
They said that if he did not stop, he would be among those who are stoned.

They told him that he had argued with them at length and to bring what he threatened if he was truthful; he replied that only God would bring it, if He willed, that they could not escape, and that his advice would not benefit them if God wished to let them go astray.

chapters.summary_md: The leaders of Nuh's people rejected him as a human being like themselves who was followed only by the lowly, and called him mad; Nuh answered that he was a messenger and a plain warner who asked no reward and would not drive away the believers [c4][c5][c7][c10][c13].
chapters.body_md:
The leaders of Nuh's people said they saw him in clear error [c1]. Nuh answered that he was not in error but a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, delivering his Lord's messages, advising them, and knowing from God what they did not know [c2]. He asked whether they were astonished that a reminder from their Lord had come on a man from among them to warn them [c3].

The leaders who disbelieved said that they saw him only as a human being like themselves [c4]. They said that only the lowliest among them followed him, and asked whether they should believe him when the lowliest followed him [c5]. They said he wished to gain superiority over them, that God would have sent down angels if He had willed, and that they had not heard of such a thing among their forefathers [c6]. They also said he was a man with madness, and that they should wait for him for a time [c7]; another passage reports that they called him mad and that he was driven off [c8].

Nuh replied that he was on a clear proof from his Lord and had been given mercy from Him, which had been hidden from them; he asked whether he could force it on them while they disliked it [c9]. He said he asked them for no wealth and that his reward was only with God, and that he would not drive away the believers, who would meet their Lord [c10]. He asked who would help him against God if he drove them away [c11]. He did not claim to hold God's treasures, to know the unseen or to be an angel, nor would he say that God would never give good to those whom they looked down on [c12]. He said he had no knowledge of what they used to do, that their reckoning was only with his Lord, and that he was only a plain warner [c13].

They said that if he did not stop, he would be among those who are stoned [c14]. They also told him that he had argued with them at length and to bring what he threatened if he was truthful; he replied that only God would bring it, if He willed, that they could not escape, and that his advice would not benefit them if God wished to let them go astray [c15].
chapters.deep_md: The objections are worded differently in each passage: that he is in error (7:60) [c1], that he is only a human being (11:27, 23:24) [c4], that the lowly follow him (11:27, 26:111) [c5], and that he is mad (23:25, 54:9) [c7][c8]. Nuh's replies are spread in the same way: his messengership (7:61-62) [c2], his proof and mercy (11:28) [c9], and his refusal to drive away the believers (11:29, 26:114) [c10].
chapters.kids_md: The leaders of Nuh's people said he was only a person like them [c4]. They said that only the lowly followed him [c5]. Nuh said he was a messenger and a warner, that he asked for no reward, and that he would not send the believers away [c2][c10][c13].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The leaders judged the message by who delivered it and who followed it: a human being like themselves, followed by people they looked down on [c4][c5]. One reading is that the passage warns against judging a message by the standing of those who follow it [c5][c10].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- The Quran does not name the leaders of Nuh's people or any individual among them or among the believers.
- It does not say how many followed Nuh or how many opposed him.
- It does not date these exchanges or give their order; the same arguments are reported in different surahs, and this chapter groups them by theme, not by time.
- The verse 11:35 (a question whether they say he invented it) is a separate aside whose speaker is not clear from the verse; it is not used here and a reviewer should decide.

claims.statement_en: Nuh stayed among his people a thousand years less fifty years.
Nuh told God that he had called his people night and day, and that his calling only increased their flight.
Nuh said that each time he called them so that God might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and were extremely arrogant.
Nuh said that he called them openly, and also spoke to them publicly and in private.

Nuh told them to ask their Lord for forgiveness, for He is ever forgiving, and said that He would then send rain upon them in abundance, increase them with wealth and sons, and give them gardens and rivers.
Nuh asked what was the matter with them that they did not look for dignity from God, when He had created them in stages.
Nuh pointed to the heavens, seven one above another, and to the moon as a light and the sun as a lamp.
Nuh reminded them that God caused them to grow from the earth, will return them into it and bring them out again, and has spread the earth for them so that they may walk its wide paths.

In another passage Nuh told his people that if his standing among them and his reminders of God's signs weighed on them, he relied on God, and they could gather their plan with their partners and act against him without giving him respite.
Nuh told them that if they turned away, he had asked them for no reward, that his reward was only with God, and that he was commanded to be among those who submit.

chapters.summary_md: Nuh stayed among his people a thousand years less fifty years, called them night and day, openly and in private, and reminded them of God's signs, but they turned away [c1][c2][c4][c7][c3].
chapters.body_md:
The Quran says Nuh stayed among his people a thousand years less fifty years [c1]. He told God he had called his people night and day, and that his calling only increased their flight [c2]. Each time he called them so that God might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and were extremely arrogant [c3]. He called them openly, and he also spoke to them publicly and in private [c4].

He told them to ask their Lord for forgiveness, for He is ever forgiving, and said that He would then send rain upon them in abundance, increase them with wealth and sons, and give them gardens and rivers [c5]. He asked what was the matter with them that they did not look for dignity from God, when He had created them in stages [c6]. He pointed to the heavens, seven one above another, and to the moon as a light and the sun as a lamp [c7]. He reminded them that God caused them to grow from the earth, will return them into it and bring them out again, and has spread the earth for them so that they may walk its wide paths [c8].

In another passage Nuh tells his people that if his standing among them and his reminders of God's signs weigh on them, he relies on God, and they may gather their plan with their partners and act against him without giving him respite [c9]. If they turn away, he has asked them for no reward; his reward is only with God, and he was commanded to be among those who submit [c10].
chapters.deep_md: The people's refusal is described by fleeing (71:6) [c2] and by blocking their ears and covering themselves (71:7) [c3]. Nuh's reminders move from his words about forgiveness and its fruits (71:10-12) [c5] to signs in the heavens and on the earth (71:15-20) [c7][c8].
chapters.kids_md: Nuh called his people for a very long time, night and day, in public and in private [c1][c2][c4]. He reminded them of the sky, the sun, the moon and the earth as signs of God [c7][c8]. But they put their fingers in their ears and would not listen [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage shows calling done in more than one manner: by night and by day, openly and privately, with encouragement and with reminders of God's signs [c2][c4][c5][c7]. One reading is that persistence in a sincere call does not depend on how it is received [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- The Quran says Nuh stayed among his people a thousand years less fifty years. It does not say whether this is his whole life or only the time he spent calling them.
- It does not say when the calling began or ended, or how the time divides among the ways of calling described here.
- The Arabic word in 71:13 (rendered 'dignity') is read in more than one way, for example as dignity given by God or as God's own majesty; this draft does not decide.
- The promises of rain, wealth, sons, gardens and rivers are reported as Nuh's words to his people; the verses do not say that anyone received them.
- The order of 10:71-72 relative to the rest is not stated.

claims.statement_en: It was revealed to Nuh that none of his people would believe except those who had already believed, so he should not be distressed by what they did.
Nuh told God that his people had disobeyed him and followed one whose wealth and children only increased his loss, and that they had plotted a great plot.
They told one another not to abandon their gods, and not to abandon Wadd, Suwa, Yaghuth, Yauq and Nasr; Nuh said they had led many astray, and asked that the wrongdoers increase only in error.
Because of their wrongs they were drowned and then made to enter a fire, and they found no helpers besides God.
Nuh asked God not to leave on the earth anyone of the disbelievers dwelling there, because if God left them they would mislead His servants and beget only wicked, ungrateful children.
Nuh asked forgiveness for himself, his parents, whoever entered his house as a believer, and the believing men and women, and asked that the wrongdoers increase only in ruin.
Nuh said that his people had denied him, and asked God to open a decisive judgement between him and them and to save him and the believers with him.
Nuh called on his Lord that he was overcome and asked for help, because they had denied him.

chapters.summary_md: God told Nuh that no more of his people would believe; Nuh complained to God of their refusal and their plotting, prayed for the believers, and asked for help [c1][c2][c6][c8].
chapters.body_md:
God revealed to Nuh that none of his people would believe except those who had already believed, and that he should not be distressed by what they did [c1]. Nuh told God that his people had disobeyed him and followed one whose wealth and children only increased his loss, and that they had plotted a great plot [c2]. They told one another not to abandon their gods, and named Wadd, Suwa, Yaghuth, Yauq and Nasr [c3]. Nuh said they had led many astray and asked that the wrongdoers increase only in error [c3].

The Quran adds that because of their wrongs they were drowned and then made to enter a fire, and that they found no helpers besides God [c4].

Nuh asked God not to leave anyone of the disbelievers dwelling on the earth, since, he said, if God left them they would mislead His servants and beget only wicked, ungrateful children [c5]. He asked forgiveness for himself, his parents, whoever entered his house as a believer, and the believing men and women, and asked that the wrongdoers increase only in ruin [c6]. In other passages he says that his people had denied him and asks God to judge decisively between them and him and to save him and the believers with him [c7]; he calls on his Lord that he is overcome and asks for help [c8].
chapters.deep_md: Nuh's requests are worded in different ways: that God judge between them and him [c7], that God help him because he is overcome [c8], and that God not leave anyone of the disbelievers dwelling on the earth [c5]. The names of the gods are given only in the passage at 71:23 [c3].
chapters.kids_md: God told Nuh that no more of his people would believe, so he should not be sad about what they did [c1]. Nuh asked God for help and to save him and the believers [c7][c8]. He asked God to forgive him, his parents and the believers [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage shows Nuh bringing his distress to God in words [c7][c8]. One reading is that taking hardship to God in prayer is presented here as the answer to rejection [c8]. In his prayer he also asks forgiveness for himself and for the believers, and not only relief [c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- The Quran does not say when, within the long period of calling, these prayers were made, or whether they came before or after the order to build the ship. This chapter groups them by theme.
- It does not say who or what these names were; the verse gives only the names as the gods the people held to. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later accounts say who they were; none is used here.
- It does not say whom the phrase 'one whose wealth and children only increased his loss' points to; it may mean a person or a kind of person.
- It does not name Nuh's parents.
- The verse 71:25 says they were drowned and then made to enter a fire; it does not say when this fire is entered or describe it.

claims.statement_en: God revealed to Nuh that none of his people would believe except those who already had, and told him to build the ship under His watch and by His revelation.
God told Nuh not to speak to Him about those who had done wrong, for they would be drowned.
While Nuh was building the ship, each time leaders of his people passed by him they mocked him.
Nuh said that if they mocked him, he would mock them in the same way, and that they would come to know who would receive a punishment that disgraces and a punishment that lasts.

chapters.summary_md: At God's command Nuh built the ship, and the leaders of his people mocked him as he built it [c1][c3].
chapters.body_md: God revealed to Nuh that none of his people would believe except those who already had, and told him to build the ship under His watch and by His revelation [c1]. He told him not to speak to Him about those who had done wrong, for they would be drowned [c2]. As Nuh built it, whenever leaders of his people passed by they mocked him [c3]. He said that if they mocked him, he would mock them in the same way, and that they would come to know who would receive a punishment that disgraces and a punishment that lasts [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The command to build the ship is worded almost alike at 11:37 and 23:27 [c1][c2]. It comes with a prohibition: Nuh is not to plead for the wrongdoers [c2].
chapters.kids_md: God told Nuh to build a ship [c1]. The leaders of his people laughed at him as he built it [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): Nuh keeps building while he is mocked [c3][c4]. One reading is that a task given by God is carried on in spite of ridicule [c1][c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- The Quran does not give the ship's size, its shape, the materials beyond those named in the next chapter, the place where it was built, or how long it took.
- It does not say what the people did, apart from mocking, while the ship was being built.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later accounts give dimensions, a building place and a timeline for the ship; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: When God's command came and the tannur (a word usually rendered oven) boiled over, God told Nuh to carry on the ship a pair of every kind, and his family, except those against whom the word had already gone out, and those who believed; few had believed with him.
Nuh told them to embark and said that in God's name was its sailing and its anchoring, for his Lord is forgiving and merciful.
God told Nuh to say, once he and those with him were settled on the ship, that praise belongs to God who had saved them from the wrongdoing people, and to ask to be landed at a blessed landing place.
God opened the gates of heaven with pouring water and made the earth burst with springs, and the waters met for a matter already decreed.
God carried Nuh on a vessel of planks and dusur (a word often rendered nails or fibres), which sailed under His watch, as a reward for one who had been rejected.
The ship sailed with them through waves like mountains.
God saved Nuh and those with him in the laden ship and drowned the rest, who had denied His signs.

chapters.summary_md: When God's command came, Nuh carried on the ship a pair of every kind, his family (except those against whom the word had gone out) and the believers; water poured from the sky and burst from the earth, and the ship sailed through waves like mountains [c1][c4][c6]. God saved Nuh and those with him and drowned the rest [c7].
chapters.body_md:
When God's command came and the tannur (a word usually rendered oven) boiled over, God told Nuh to carry on the ship a pair of every kind, and his family, except those against whom the word had already gone out, and those who believed; few had believed with him [c1]. Nuh told them to embark and said that in God's name was its sailing and its anchoring, for his Lord is forgiving and merciful [c2]. God told Nuh to say, once he and those with him were settled on the ship, that praise belongs to God who had saved them from the wrongdoing people, and to ask to be landed at a blessed landing place [c3].

The Quran describes the flood in these terms: God opened the gates of heaven with pouring water and made the earth burst with springs, and the waters met for a matter already decreed [c4]. He carried Nuh on a vessel of planks and dusur (a word often rendered nails or fibres), which sailed under His watch, as a reward for one who had been rejected [c5]. It sailed with them through waves like mountains [c6]. God saved Nuh and those with him in the laden ship and drowned the rest [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The flood is told from different sides: the sign and the command to embark [c1], Nuh's words on boarding [c2][c3], the description of the waters [c4], the vessel [c5] and the waves [c6]. The outcome is the same in every passage that tells it: Nuh and those with him are saved and the rest are drowned [c7].
chapters.kids_md: When God's command came, water poured from the sky and sprang up from the earth [c4]. Nuh took on the ship a pair of every kind, his family (except those about whom God's word had gone out), and the believers [c1]. The ship sailed through waves like mountains [c6]. God saved Nuh and those with him [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): Nuh's words on boarding give thanks to God for rescue and ask for a blessed landing [c2][c3]. One reading is that gratitude and prayer are joined at the moment of safety [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- The Quran does not say what the tannur was or where it was; 'oven' is a common rendering and its sense is discussed.
- It does not say how many people were on the ship, which animals were carried or how many kinds, or how they were gathered and cared for.
- It does not say how long the flood lasted, how deep the water rose, or whether the water covered the whole earth or only the region of Nuh's people. A scholar should decide how to word the extent for readers.
- The Arabic word dusur is explained as nails and as fibres; this draft does not decide.
- Which members of Nuh's family were taken and which were not is not stated beyond 'those against whom the word had gone out'; the next chapter tells of his son.
- The Quran does not name the passengers.

claims.statement_en: Nuh called out to his son, who was standing apart, to come aboard with them and not to be with the disbelievers.

The son said he would take refuge on a mountain that would protect him from the water; Nuh replied that nothing that day protects from God's command except for the one on whom He has mercy; the wave came between them, and the son was among the drowned.
Nuh called to his Lord, saying that his son was of his family, that God's promise is true, and that He is the most just of judges.
God answered that the son was not of Nuh's family, that his deed was not righteous, and that Nuh should not ask Him about what he had no knowledge of; God advised him not to be among the ignorant.
Nuh said that he sought refuge in God from asking what he had no knowledge of, and that unless God forgave him and had mercy on him he would be among the losers.

chapters.summary_md: Nuh called to his son to board; the son refused, the wave came between them and he was drowned [c1][c2]. Nuh appealed to God about him, God answered that he was not of Nuh's family because his deed was not righteous, and Nuh asked forgiveness [c3][c4][c5].
chapters.body_md:
As the ship sailed through the waves, Nuh called out to his son, who was standing apart, to come aboard with them and not to be with the disbelievers [c1]. The son said he would take refuge on a mountain that would protect him from the water [c2]. Nuh replied that nothing that day protects from God's command except for the one on whom He has mercy; then the wave came between them, and the son was among the drowned [c2].

Nuh called to his Lord, saying that his son was of his family, that God's promise is true, and that He is the most just of judges [c3]. God answered that the son was not of Nuh's family, that his deed was not righteous, and that Nuh should not ask Him about what he had no knowledge of; God advised him not to be among the ignorant [c4]. Nuh said that he sought refuge in God from asking what he had no knowledge of, and that unless God forgave him and had mercy on him he would be among the losers [c5].
chapters.deep_md: God's answer in 11:46 gives a reason for the statement that the son is not of Nuh's family: his deed was not righteous [c4]. The passage ends with Nuh asking forgiveness for the question itself [c5].
chapters.kids_md: Nuh called to his son to come on the ship, but the son would not come and was among those drowned [c1][c2]. Nuh asked God about his son, and God told him not to ask about what he did not know [c3][c4]. Nuh asked God to forgive him [c5].
